    The representation of a quiver carried by a module over its path algebra #

    LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.ModuleDecomposition equips a left module M over the path algebra kQ of a finite quiver with the data of a representation of Q: the k-subspace eᵥ M = LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexComponent k M v at each vertex, the k-linear map LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.pathMap along each path, and the restriction LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexComponentMap of a kQ-linear map to those subspaces. This file assembles that data into an object and a morphism of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep k Q, bundles the assignment as a functor ModuleCat (kQ) ⥤ LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep k Q, and proves that functor fully faithful.

    Main definitions #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepOfModule k Q M: the representation v ↦ eᵥ M of Q carried by a kQ-module.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepHomOfModule k Q f: the morphism of representations carried by a kQ-linear map.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepHomComponent k Q φ v: the component at v of a morphism between two such representations, retyped as a map eᵥ M →ₗ[k] eᵥ N.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.moduleHomOfQuiverRepHom k Q φ: the kQ-linear map glued from those components, inverse to LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepHomOfModule.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepFunctor k Q: the two previous assignments bundled as a functor ModuleCat (kQ) ⥤ LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep k Q, and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepFunctorFullyFaithful: its full faithfulness.

    Main results #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_quiverRepOfModule: the dimension vector of quiverRepOfModule k Q M is v ↦ dimₖ (eᵥ M), and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.finrank_eq_sum_dimVector_quiverRepOfModule: over a finite-dimensional module its coordinates sum to dimₖ M.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepHomOfModule_id and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepHomOfModule_comp: the assignment is functorial.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepHomOfModule_injective and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepHomOfModule_moduleHomOfQuiverRepHom: it is injective and surjective on Hom-sets, packaged as LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepHomOfModule_bijective and, on the bundled functor, as LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepFunctorFullyFaithful. The inverse laws for the explicit inverse are that surjectivity statement together with LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.moduleHomOfQuiverRepHom_quiverRepHomOfModule.
    • The functor is additive and k-linear, so that on Hom-sets it is an isomorphism of k-vector spaces and not merely a bijection; that is what makes a dimension computed for representations also one for kQ-modules.

    Implementation notes #

    Both the module and the resulting representation are described through the subspaces eᵥ M of M, not through an abstract direct-sum carrier; that is what makes LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexProjection and the identity ∑ᵥ eᵥ • x = x (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sum_coe_vertexProjection), both from LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.ModuleDecomposition, available, and those two carry the whole content of full faithfulness: injectivity is the fact that a kQ-linear map is determined by its restrictions to the components, and surjectivity glues the components of a morphism back together, the naturality in the paths being exactly what makes the glued map kQ-linear.

    The vertex set is finite throughout, as it must be: the unit 1 = ∑ᵥ eᵥ of kQ is a finite sum of vertex idempotents, and without it a module is not the sum of its vertex components at all. It is carried as [Finite Q], refined to [Fintype Q] only where a sum over the vertices is genuinely in a statement; elsewhere Fintype.ofFinite supplies the enumeration a proof or a body needs. The base is a field only because LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep is; the underlying data of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.ModuleDecomposition needs no more than a commutative semiring. The k-linear structure carried on M alongside the kQ-action is asked for as [Module k M] with [IsScalarTower k (pathAlgebra k Q) M], not extracted from the algebra, exactly as in that file. The three modules of the morphism section share one universe, since ModuleCat k — and hence LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep k Q — has objects in a single universe. Those two hypotheses are what forces the source category of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepFunctor to be spelled with the scoped instances ModuleCat.moduleOfAlgebraModule and ModuleCat.isScalarTower_of_algebra_moduleCat of Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Algebra, which restrict the scalars of an object of ModuleCat (kQ) along algebraMap k (kQ); a file stating anything about that functor must open scoped ModuleCat for the same reason.

    A representation is a functor out of CategoryTheory.Paths Q, whose objects are the vertices of Q only after unfolding the semireducible CategoryTheory.Paths. Two devices from the neighbouring files handle that: change Q at v restates a quantified object as a vertex, and the functorial equations of quiverRepOfModule are proved by first naming the intended identity with the vertex-indexed LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.pathMap_nil and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.pathMap_comp, whose statements are then matched definitionally. The morphism-level API is stated on ModuleCat homomorphisms rather than on elements for the same reason: an element of (quiverRepOfModule k Q M).obj v is an element of eᵥ M only up to unfolding, so a coercion of it to M does not elaborate. That is what LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepHomComponent is for: it names the component of a morphism at the vertex-indexed type eᵥ M →ₗ[k] eᵥ N once and for all, and everything about the gluing is stated through it.

    References #

    This is the fully faithful half of quiverRepEquivalence, Layer 1 of TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/QuiverRepresentations/README.md, which asks for the equivalence "sending a module M to the representation v ↦ eᵥ M, with an arrow acting by left multiplication, and inverting through the idempotent decomposition M = ⨁ᵥ eᵥ M". Full faithfulness is proved here; the essential surjectivity that completes the equivalence — a kQ-module structure on ⨁ᵥ Mᵥ for a given representation — is LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.Representation.AsModule, where the two halves are assembled into LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepEquivalence.

    The equivalence itself is classical; see Assem--Simson--Skowroński, Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras I, Ch. III, or Schiffler, Quiver Representations, Ch. 5.

    The representation of Q carried by a module over its path algebra: the vector space at a vertex v is the component eᵥ M, and a path acts by left multiplication, carrying the component at its source to the component at its target.

                The functor is k-linear: the vertex components of a kQ-module are k-subspaces, and restricting a kQ-linear map to them is k-linear in the map. This is what makes the functor compare k-dimensions of morphism spaces.
